fields.name: enable
fields.description: Global controller enable. When 0, request issuance and actuator command validity are inhibited.

fields.name: slew_enable
fields.description: Enables slew-rate limiting on accepted actuator commands.

fields.name: response_accept_enable
fields.description: Enables acceptance of validated response packets.

fields.name: fault_clear
fields.description: Write-1-to-clear sticky fault latches that are software-clearable.

fields.name: timeout_limit
fields.description: Maximum response latency in clock cycles before timeout fault is asserted.

fields.name: cmd_min
fields.description: Minimum allowed actuator command after clamping.

fields.name: cmd_max
fields.description: Maximum allowed actuator command after clamping.

fields.name: slew_limit
fields.description: Maximum absolute command delta per accepted update when slew_enable is set.

fields.name: current_request_seq
fields.description: Current outstanding request sequence identifier.

fields.name: current_request_id
fields.description: Current outstanding request identifier.

fields.name: request_pending
fields.description: Indicates an outstanding request is waiting for validation.

fields.name: response_valid
fields.description: Indicates a validated response was accepted in the last update.

fields.name: stale_fault
fields.description: Latched stale or sequence-mismatch fault.

fields.name: timeout_fault
fields.description: Latched timeout fault.

fields.name: clamp_active
fields.description: Indicates the accepted command was clamped in the last update.

fields.name: fault_latched
fields.description: Aggregate latched fault indication.

fields.name: seq_counter
fields.description: Monotonic or wrapping sequence counter used for request generation and validation.

fields.name: request_count
fields.description: Count of issued requests.

fields.name: response_count
fields.description: Count of accepted responses.

fields.name: last_accepted_cmd
fields.description: Most recently accepted and limited actuator command.

fields.name: fault_status
fields.description: Bit-encoded fault summary exposed on the top-level fault_status port.

sources.name: FAULT_IRQ
sources.description: Optional software-notification source implied by latched fault status. Not a required top-level port.

init_sequence: Hold rst_n low, then release high.
Write CTRL with ENABLE=0, SLEW_ENABLE=0, RESPONSE_ACCEPT_ENABLE=1, FAULT_CLEAR=0 to establish conservative defaults.
Program TIMEOUT_THR, CMD_MIN, CMD_MAX, and SLEW_LIMIT as required by the application.
Write CTRL with ENABLE=1 when the system is ready to issue requests.
polling_sequence: Poll STATUS for REQUEST_PENDING, RESPONSE_VALID, STALE_FAULT, TIMEOUT_FAULT, CLAMP_ACTIVE, FAULT_LATCHED, and FALLBACK_ACTIVE.
Read REQUEST_SEQ, REQUEST_ID, SEQ_COUNT, REQUEST_COUNT, RESPONSE_COUNT, CMD_LAST, and FAULT_STATUS for telemetry.
If FAULT_LATCHED is set, write CTRL.FAULT_CLEAR=1 to clear software-clearable sticky faults, then re-read STATUS.
irq_sequence: If fault notification is implemented in the system integration, service the fault event by reading STATUS and FAULT_STATUS.
If the fault is software-clearable, write CTRL.FAULT_CLEAR=1 and confirm the fault bits are deasserted before re-enabling operation.

consistency_notes: All assumptions remain compatible with DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.
The register map is firmware-visible through the declared MMIO control interface with mmio_valid, mmio_write, mmio_addr, mmio_wdata, mmio_rdata, and mmio_ready.
No incompatible hierarchy, bus protocol, or top-level ports are invented.
No fallback command or substitute actuator output is defined; invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions inhibit actuator validity and latch faults for software handling.
Register names, addresses, fields, access, and bit ranges are enforced from DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.register_contract.
